title: [spec-gap][R-06-204/R-06-205] OSCORE context bound (≤64) + LRU eviction divergent across stacks
description:
spec/06-security.md §8.8: 'Implementations MUST bound OSCORE security contexts to at most 64 entries. On overflow, implementations MUST evict the least-recently-used context (LRU by last message timestamp).'

Evidence (sweep 2026-09-01, docs/spec-coverage/06-security-part2.md):
- C: bound ≤64 OK (lichen/subsys/lichen/oscore/Kconfig:20-23 LICHEN_OSCORE_MAX_CONTEXTS default 8, range 2-32) but NO eviction — full table returns OSCORE_ERR_NO_MEMORY (oscore_ctx.c:379-388).
- Python: LRU eviction exists (channel.py:416-435 _evict_peer_contexts_if_needed) but bound is _MAX_ACTIVE_PEER_CONTEXTS=2048 > 64 (channel.py:144).
- Rust node: contexts HashMap unbounded, no eviction (rust/lichen-node/src/secure.rs:443, inserts :565/:579).

human-only: oscore internals have the human-only edit bar; do not plan an agent fix. Question for mark: align spec to implementations (raise 64, drop LRU mandate) or align implementations to spec?
